source_snapshot.procedure: Populate all drives, boot, verify RAID-controller status, remove one selected drive, wait 30 seconds, reinsert it and repeat ten cycles.
source_snapshot.criteria: The drive remains correctly detected in MSM and BMC logs show the expected events without unexpected errors.

historical_reviews.deepseek: Correctly refuses remote bay action but treats OS enumeration as sufficient and truncates the very logs needed to detect delayed RAID errors.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: Restores the populated-backplane, 30-second wait, ten-cycle, MSM and BMC checkpoints with stop-on-degrade safeguards.
historical_reviews.related_cases: Row89 hot-adds a drive into an empty-at-boot slot once; this row removes and reinserts an existing selected drive ten times from a populated RAID system.
historical_reviews.v3_1: Each cycle must reach an approved stable array state before another physical action; completion count alone cannot override a rebuild or degraded state.

original_test_intent: Verify that one approved drive in a populated backplane can be removed and reinserted after 30 seconds for ten cycles while remaining correctly identified in MSM/RAID and producing correct BMC/OS records without storage failure.
original_method: A qualified operator performs the exact physical cycle on one stable-identity drive while the agent captures complete array, drive, OS and BMC state before and after every action and permits continuation only when approved health gates remain clear.
manual_activity: User approves the exact array/member/cycle and recovery plan; qualified operator performs ten timed remove/reinsert actions; agent monitors and records every state transition without actuating hardware.
required_inputs: RAID controller/MSM version, RAID level, virtual/physical disk topology and protection state
Selected drive serial/slot/backplane map and supported hot-plug procedure
Rebuild, patrol, cache, spare and cycle-continuation policy
Backup/data-integrity plan, 30-second timing and ten-cycle maintenance window
Qualified operator, OOB/console, BMC access, abort thresholds and recovery owner
safety_requirements: Begin only from a healthy protected array with no rebuild, patrol conflict or predictive failure
Confirm the selected member and slot before every removal and remove no other drive
Wait the full specified 30 seconds and verify stable controller state after reinsertion before the next cycle
Preserve complete logs and stop on wrong identity, degraded/rebuild/unconfigured state, media/filesystem/boot/thermal/power/BMC fault or access loss
Never force online, rebuild, repair, power a bay, reboot or retry automatically
agent_execution_scope: Capture full MSM/controller virtual and physical disk baseline plus stable slot mapping
Timestamp each operator removal and reinsertion and collect complete per-cycle array/OS/BMC/health evidence
Enforce approved abort gates and verify the final drive/array/data state
Do not manipulate hardware or RAID recovery and do not issue verdict
engineer_actions: Approve the array/member, hot-plug, timing, cycle and recovery matrix
Provide a qualified operator and own any degraded/rebuild/data recovery decision
Review all ten cycle records and final data/array evidence and decide PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: lsblk can corroborate OS visibility, but insecure SSH and tail-only dmesg cannot prove MSM controller identity, RAID state, per-cycle transitions, BMC events or final array health.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use the approved full MSM/vendor RAID inventory plus stable OS identity, health and complete BMC/OS logs before removal, after removal and after reinsertion for each numbered cycle.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Populated backplane, one selected drive, 30-second wait, exactly ten cycles, MSM/BMC checks and source 80/10 timing fields are preserved.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Treat every remove/reinsert as an individually gated RAID state transition with stable identity, complete logs and no continuation from an abnormal state.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds explicit array protection, per-cycle abort logic and final data-health proof while preserving all ten physical cycles.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Automation monitors and documents; the qualified operator retains every physical action and the engineer owns recovery/verdict.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Controllers may start rebuild or copyback asynchronously after reinsertion, so simple reappearance cannot authorize the next cycle.

project_override_considerations: If the selected device is a non-redundant, boot-critical or cache/protection member, the cycle is not safe until an engineer approves an alternate protected configuration; RAID assumptions must not be inferred.
expected_evidence: Critical approval and vendor backplane/RAID hot-plug procedure
Full controller/MSM, array, firmware and serial-to-slot baseline
Operator identity plus ten removal, 30-second wait and reinsertion timestamps/photos
Per-cycle physical/virtual disk state, rebuild/background-job, health/temperature and complete OS/BMC logs
Final healthy array, drive mapping, boot/filesystem/data-integrity and management state

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The Master source consistently defines a ten-cycle RAID hot-plug test. DeepSeek's limited evidence is incomplete but does not make source identity or intent ambiguous.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Array, operator and recovery controls are critical execution prerequisites that can be supplied; the review itself is complete.

review_improvement: Makes each of the ten physical cycles independently traceable to exact RAID state and stops progression on degradation instead of relying on OS reappearance.
independent_technical_reasoning: A reinserted RAID member can enumerate while the controller is still degraded, rebuilding, foreign or predictive-fail. Repeating removal during that transient can destroy redundancy, so every cycle needs controller-level stable-state evidence, complete delayed logs and a hard gate before the next action; lsblk alone is not a safety or acceptance signal.
